name: local-ai-mcp
description: Run, fit, and route work to local LLMs: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Docker Model Runner, MLX, vLLM, Foundry Local.
long_description: An operations-first control plane for the models on your own machine. Discover what is installed and loaded across runtimes, check what fits your GPU (exact KV-cache sizing, multi-GPU, Apple Silicon unified memory), pull/load/unload models, and delegate completions or embeddings to the best local model with one call. Inference never goes to a hosted API unless you configure one and name it explicitly.

vllm_api_key.title: vLLM API key (optional)
vllm_api_key.description: Only if vLLM was started with --api-key

foundry_local_host.title: Foundry Local URL (optional)
foundry_local_host.description: http://localhost:<port>, with the port from `foundry service status`

openai_compat_api_key.title: OpenAI-compatible server API key (optional)
openai_compat_api_key.description: Bearer token for the server above

moonshot_api_key.title: Moonshot AI (Kimi) API key (optional, hosted)
moonshot_api_key.description: Hosted: only used when a tool names provider "moonshot", unless hosted fallback is on

allow_hosted_fallback.title: Allow hosted fallback
allow_hosted_fallback.description: Let calls without a provider use hosted providers (off keeps inference local)

disabled_providers.title: Skip runtimes (optional)
disabled_providers.description: Comma-separated provider names not to probe, e.g. lmstudio,dockermodelrunner

extra_providers.title: Extra provider instances (optional, JSON)
extra_providers.description: JSON array of {type, host, name?, apiKey?, kind?}, e.g. a second Ollama on your LAN

benchmark_cache.title: Benchmark results file (optional)
benchmark_cache.description: Where benchmark speeds are kept for delegate ranking. Leave blank for the per-user cache dir; "off" disables.

tools.name: list_providers
tools.description: List configured model runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Docker Model Runner, and any opt-in MLX / vLLM / Foundry Local / OpenAI-compatible / hosted instances) with host, kind (local or hosted), live status, and capabilities.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List models installed/available on each live provider, keyed by provider. Pass provider to query just one.

tools.name: list_loaded
tools.description: List models currently loaded into memory on each live provider, with VRAM use and context length where the runtime reports them.

tools.name: model_info
tools.description: Detailed metadata for one model (family, parameter size, quantization, context length, and layer architecture where available). Without provider, queries the live local providers that have the model.

tools.name: pull_model
tools.description: HEAVY: Download a model onto ONE provider (multiple GB, can take a long time). Streams download progress via MCP progress notifications when the client sends a progressToken. Without provider, uses the provider that already has the model, else the first live local provider that can pull.

tools.name: remove_model
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: Permanently delete a model from one provider. provider is REQUIRED (no fan-out). If the client supports elicitation the user is asked to confirm directly; otherwise confirm:true is required.

tools.name: load_model
tools.description: Load a model into memory on ONE provider so it is ready for inference. Optional keepAlive (e.g. '5m', '1h') and contextLength. Without provider, uses the live local provider that has the model.

tools.name: unload_model
tools.description: Unload a model from memory to free VRAM/RAM on ONE provider. Without provider, uses the live local provider that has it loaded.

tools.name: ensure_model
tools.description: Make a model ready in one call: optionally pull it, check it fits current free VRAM, unload other models if needed (evict: 'lru' or 'all'), load it, and verify. Use dryRun:true to get the plan without changing anything.

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Check whether each provider is reachable and report its version (and live metrics such as vLLM KV-cache usage). Without provider, checks every configured provider, including hosted ones.

tools.name: system_resources
tools.description: Report local hardware: platform, total/available RAM, CPU count, and GPUs with total/free VRAM (NVIDIA via nvidia-smi, AMD/Intel via sysfs or the Windows registry, Apple Silicon unified memory). Each GPU names its data source.

tools.name: fit_check
tools.description: Will a model run on this machine, and where? Uses the installed model's size and exact layer architecture when the runtime exposes it (else parameter-count or catalog estimates) to size weights + KV cache for a context length, then compares with free VRAM summed across GPUs and available RAM. Returns target gpu / partial (GPU+CPU split) / cpu / none, with the numbers and how the KV estimate was made. Credits back memory the model already uses if it is loaded.

tools.name: benchmark
tools.description: HEAVY: Runs REAL inference. Measures a model on this machine with a warmup (absorbs load time) plus N streamed runs: time-to-first-token, generation tokens/sec (runtime-reported when available, else measured after the first token), and prompt-processing speed. Pass models[] to compare several models with the same prompt, ranked by generation speed.

tools.name: search_available
tools.description: Search the built-in curated catalog of well-known local models (Ollama tags) by name, family, or task. Offline and instant. For live results with per-quant fit, use search_models with source 'huggingface'.

tools.name: suggest_model
tools.description: Recommend catalog models for a task, ranked for THIS machine: fully-on-GPU first, then partial GPU offload, then CPU-only. Within a tier the largest (most capable) model comes first unless preferSpeed is true. Flags models already installed on a live provider and explains each pick.

tools.name: search_models
tools.description: Find models to download, annotated with whether each fits this machine. source 'huggingface' searches GGUF repos on the Hugging Face Hub and returns per-quant sizes, the best quant for this hardware, and pullable references (Ollama: hf.co/<repo>:<quant>). source 'catalog' searches the offline curated list. The Ollama library has no public search API, so it is not a source.

tools.name: complete
tools.description: DELEGATED INFERENCE: Offload a completion to a model you choose for cost savings and privacy. Without provider, runs on the live LOCAL provider that has the model (never a hosted API unless LOCAL_AI_ALLOW_HOSTED_FALLBACK is set); the result's 'provider', 'host' and 'local' fields say where it ran. Supports system prompts, JSON / JSON-Schema output (validated 'parsed' field), seed/topP/topK, image inputs for vision models, and contextLength for long inputs. Streams tokens via MCP progress notifications when the client sends a progressToken.

tools.name: embed
tools.description: DELEGATED EMBEDDINGS: Generate embeddings for a string or an array of texts. Without provider, runs on the live local provider that has the model. Always returns one vector per input.

tools.name: delegate
tools.description: ONE CALL to offload work locally: pick the best model for a task on THIS machine, make it ready, and run it. Prefers models already loaded (no load cost), then installed models that fit your free VRAM, then (with allowPull) the best catalog model that fits. Task specialists (coder, vision, reasoning) win over general models; then larger fitting models win, grouped into size tiers (within ~20% parameter count); inside a tier, the model benchmarked fastest on this machine wins (run benchmark to record speeds; results expire after 14 days). Never uses a hosted provider unless allowHosted is true. Returns the completion plus a 'routing' block explaining the choice.
